snippet.title: Be a Better Communicator: 5 Conversation Commandments from the Best Communication Books
snippet.description:
1-Page Summary: https://tinyurl.com/5-c-commandmentss
Productivity Game Academy: https://tinyurl.com/academyPG

You’ll have over 100,000 conversations in your lifetime. Why not get really good at them? After all, every friendship, partnership, and job offer begins with a conversation. Yet, most conversation advice is vague and terrible.

That's why I dove into the greatest communication books to find five specific, practical techniques that actually work. I call them the 5 Conversation Commandments.

In this video, you'll learn:
- How to be genuinely interested in people with the FORD method
- The secret to maximizing your charisma with the "flooding smile" technique
- Why being slightly unexpected and playful is the key to a memorable conversation
- How to ask DEEP questions that build an instant connection
- The simple practice that makes others feel heard and valued

The 5 Conversation Commandments:
1. Thou shall be genuinely interested.
2. Thou shall maximize their charisma.
3. Thou shall be slightly unexpected.
4. Thou shall ask deep questions.
5. Thou shall make others feel heard.

Resources Mentioned:
How to Win Friends and Influence People by Dale Carnegie
The Charisma Myth by Olivia Fox Cabane
How to Talk to Anyone by Leil Lowndes
Supercommunicators by Charles Duhigg
Just Listen by Mark Goulston

Improve your social skills and change your life, one conversation at a time. What’s the single best piece of conversation advice you've ever received? Share it in the comments below!

✅ Spot and eliminate hidden waste
✅ Remove the one constraint that’s holding everything back
✅ Identify and double down on bright spots of success

📚 Based on insights from Reset by Dan Heath (author of Switch and Made to Stick), you’ll learn how to create focused breakthroughs—without working harder.

🎯 You’ll see how a hospital cut patient steps by 91%, how Chick-fil-A doubled drive-thru speed, and how noticing one habit saved a failing marriage. These aren’t just stories—they’re playbooks you can use to change your own life, work, or team.

🔍 Topics covered:
• Mapping waste with Spaghetti Charts
• Bottleneck thinking (with the 1-question bottleneck test)
• How to uncover bright spots and build systems around what’s working
• The “Focus Burst” method to drive fast, lasting progress

snippet.description:
Full briefing w/ Agent Owner Card: https://natesnewsletter.substack.com/p/ai-agent-ownership?r=1z4sm5&utm_campaign=post&utm_medium=web&showWelcomeOnShare=true

AI agent ownership is the skill most teams skip in 2026. Once an agent reads real files and does real work, somebody has to own it, and most people cannot say who.

My Links 🔗
👉🏻 Newsletter: https://natesnewsletter.substack.com/
👉🏻 X: https://x.com/natebjones

The common story is that agents are confusing because nobody agrees on the definition. The real question is who owns the work once the agent starts doing it.

In this video, I share the inside scoop on what agent ownership actually looks like:

 - Why a working agent stops being a tool and becomes your responsibility
 - How to tell an assistant chat from a real agent job
 - What care and feeding means for an agent you depend on
 - Where unowned team agents fail and who should catch them

Agents are useful enough to run real work now, which is exactly why the teams that name an owner for each one pull ahead of the teams collecting demos.

snippet.title: I Connected Claude to Everything. Then I Saw the Gap.
snippet.description:
🧲 Grab my free Claude Connector Verification Checklist, the 5 steps I use to catch what Claude misses: https://bit.ly/4wiTzLa

I connected Claude to my calendar, my inbox, and my notes. Then I found out how little it really sees.

Connectors give your Second Brain a nervous system. Senses that pull context in from your apps, so you stop copying and pasting. The first time it works, it feels like magic.

But here's the catch most people miss: when Claude connects to a tool like Notion, it doesn't read everything. It samples a small slice of your data, often half a percent to five percent, skewed toward what's recent. That gap creates an illusion of authority, a confident answer built on a sliver of the evidence.

This video is the short version: the 5 checks I run to verify Claude's work, and the habits that keep my setup safe and lean. No demos, just the rules I follow.
